newsitem.title: UK: BTR shares rise as profits beat forecasts.
newsitem.headline: BTR shares rise as profits beat forecasts.

text.p: Shares in industrial conglomerate BTR Plc rose in early trading on Thursday after profits topped analyst expectations.
The stock was up 11p at 263-1/2 by 0806 GMT.
Pre-tax profits dropped to 1.30 billion stg from 1.50 billion a year before, but that compared with analyst expectations in a wide range between 728 million stg and 1.25 billion.

Dealers said the stock had also been boosted by the company's comment that it had no current need for further share issues and could even see circumstances in which it would be advantageous to buy back warrants or shares.

"The results and statement are reasonably upbeat, the stock has already had a bit of a recovery and it could go further," said one dealer. "Having been a real dog it is starting to look a bit better."
Chief executive Ian Strachan said 1996 had been a year of "significant change" which had set the course for significant future growth.

He said BTR's progress would depend on the growth of key markets and would be "somewhat impacted by currency translation" but he expected the underlying performance "to improve steadily in 1997 as our strategy is implemented."
BTR shares, which hit a 1997 low of 236p on February 28, were up 9p at 261-1/2 by 0838 GMT, in volume of 1.9 million shares.
